utterances.text: Did you have a conversation - thank you - with Ratko Nikolic about your father?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that he found him in prison when he arrived there, that he found him in prison and they were in prison together. And then my father asked him, How come you're here, Ratko? And he said, Well, they've caught me too. And then my father asked him, Ratko, have you seen my sisters? And he asked about some other people. And Ratko said, No, I haven't seen anyone. And then Ratko told me - and I omitted to mention this previously - how they had beaten them in prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's precisely why this witness shouldn't be giving evidence about -- relaying a conversation of someone who was here giving evidence before this Court. Really, in my submission, it would be completely inappropriate for Ratko Nikolic's evidence to be given twice --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the other witness was asked whether he had any discussions about this one, and do you remember what he said?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, I don't recall offhand, Your Honour. But my concern is that this witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He was asked precisely also in relation to some particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Precisely, Your Honour. But this witness, it's clear, is about to recount Ratko Nikolic's treatment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, no. That's not going to be the case --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: -- which we can't cross-examine on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's not going to be the case. Yes, let's proceed, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, one last question with respect to this document. Are you familiar with the person Hasan Hasic? On page 48 of this document -- well, it's page 31 on the B/C/S version --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You mean do I know this person?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Is this person familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know this person. I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have any more questions with respect to the documents, and at this time I would ask that this document be tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It has already been tendered and given a number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Oh, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, with respect to your grandfather, did you ever see him alive after you left the village of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't learn anything until Kravica was liberated. That's when we found him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us about the circumstances surrounding the location of your grandfather.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My grandfather was found behind the school, behind the school where coal was kept. Nego Eric was found there, Kristina Eric, his wife. And the fourth person was Obackic; I don't know whether her name was Milja or Ljubica. I found the four of them behind the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say you found the four of them, you're referring to finding their bodies; correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, their bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the ages of the other people -- the other three individuals who were found with your father, if you know? Your grandfather, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were older than my grandfather. They were about 80 years old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many people died in the Kravica attack?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. Forty-seven, 47 were killed on Christmas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were these men and women?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 47 altogether were killed in Kravica on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just going back to your grandfather for a moment, did you examine the bodies, did you take a look at the bodies yourself?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. We arrived there, five or six of us; they were family and neighbours of mine. And we took them out of this coal shed, out onto the meadow. And I could see very well that my grandfather's throat had been cut, and that his -- a part of his arm was missing. Nego Eric had something tied round his throat. And as for those two women, I couldn't see anything on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of these bodies or individuals, were they in military clothing? And could you tell us if the bodies were preserved, the condition -- I'll rephrase that. Could you tell us whether any of the bodies were in military uniform?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My grandfather had mining boots, he had a suit on, he had a white shirt and a pullover, and he had a cap on when he stayed behind in Kravica. And we found everything on him except the cap.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the other bodies, do you recall what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Including your father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Including your father. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those bodies, Nego and all the others, my father [as interpreted] had olive-drab canvas trousers, and the upper part was an old JNA uniform. But when we found him in Kravica, he was naked to the waist. I forgot to mention that I found a document in his pocket - the doctor found it - and it said on the document "Taken prisoner, the 7th of January in Kravica; died on the 6th of February 1993." We found this in his pocket. And there was nothing on the upper part of his body. I asked the doctor if he'd had anything on him. The doctor said no, he had been naked to the waist, but he did have his trousers on and his belt. All the people who died, none of them were in uniform. People could recognise their relatives by the clothes they had on, because they'd been in Kravica, not buried for almost two months. Animals had already started eating them. So you could recognise them mostly by the clothes they had on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. With respect to the attack on Kravica, did you speak with anyone and did you get any information about -- I'll rephrase that, Your Honour. Did there come a time that you spoke to a Dodo Peric?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I spoke to Djordjo Peric and to Miladin Popovic, people who remained in Kravica that day and arrived on the following day, who had no chance to get out of Kravica. And Djordjo Peric slept the whole night in a shaft that was used for sewage. And he spent the entire night there. Miladin Popovic also stayed at his home. He wasn't able to get out so he hid. And Djordjo told me, when they entered the houses, first they took out food, then they started setting fire to the houses. He had to get out of where he was hiding. And then he told me how they had celebrated, how they had sung a song mentioning Naser Oric and fired shots, and then he managed to get out and -- get out alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "they," who are you referring to? Did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Mr. Peric tell you -- describe the Muslims to you, what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He said they all had the same kind of uniform. They had automatic rifles. He watched them set fire to the houses. The house of Drago Radovic specifically, the house of Bozo Radovic, Dragan Radovic, Ljubo Jovanovic, Ceto Vasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long was he able to hide in the town; did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He remained hidden throughout the night of the 7th of January and the whole of the next day. It was only after the army had withdrawn that he came out. Once the army had left Kravica, towards the evening, he left and he came to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you speak with anyone regarding the battle that had taken place or -- excuse me, the attack that had taken place in the forest between Kravica and Jezero?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said a while ago the first victim fell at about 8.00 when the siren was sounded and the people headed for Jezero. They left the bakery and went up for Jezero. They were outside the school building and left for Jezero. After about 45 minutes, they came back with Milovan Nikolic's body. He had been wounded at some point between Kravica and Jezero, and he died outside the school building in Kravica. The Muslims then withdrew behind the line and waited there. He remained in the school building and the school building burned down. After Kravica had been liberated, I personally went to the school building. I found my grandfather there, and he was burned inside the school building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Richardson, please try to finish within the next 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm getting there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you, describe to you what the attackers were wearing?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to make the following observation which is that it's not just a question of witnesses giving hearsay evidence where we don't -- and I know that that's not in itself an objection, but when one has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was going to intervene and asked -- because Ms. Richardson asked who did you -- did you speak to other people, did they tell you. He never mentions any names.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No. It's not only that, but we have -- it seems to be witness after witness who comes to The Hague and then pulls a rabbit out of a hat and mentions some person who apparently will never be a Prosecution witness, who apparently has all sorts of incredibly useful information. And it's something which is something which is a surprise tactic to the extent that we have never heard of these people before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But at the end of the day, you report you so well --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Exactly. But if at least to minimise the prejudice, if my learned friend could try and pin down to specifically who said what and when, so we actually have some grasp on what's being purported.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Also, to know whether these persons will be coming over. Who were these persons who gave you all these details about the attack? Who were they? Who did you speak to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] People from Kravica who brought him over. For example, Zeljko Odovic, I know this man personally. He was there. Zeljko Odovic, Rade Dadic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are these persons alive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they're alive. One lives and works in Russia, and the other is in Bratunac, he works in the school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which one is in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zeljko Odovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyone else you spoke to that gave you all these details, or some of these details?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When they left, when they left for Jezero, when they headed for the defence line. And in about 45 minutes to one hour, they came back with a wounded man. They came outside the school building and took him inside the school in Kravica. He stayed there and he burned down there. When we collected the bodies in Kravica, where my grandfather was buried and the three or four civilians, it wasn't 10 metres from there in one of the rooms inside of the school building. We collected all the bones and brought it to the place where all the bodies of the victims had been collected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what these individuals whom you just named told you about what had happened in the forest between Kravica and Jezero? I'll rephrase that question. I think you had already told us, but I believe my question was with respect to what these attackers were wearing. Were you told?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And by which individual, please.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had white uniforms. They were lying in the snow, and when they came by, they started firing and they shot Milovan Nikolic; they wounded him. A bullet had passed straight through, right here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those people who brought him over from where he was wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zeljko Odovic, Rade Dadic, and two other persons whose names escape me now. They brought him to the school building and he died there in front of our very eyes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Next question, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. At this time I'd like to show some photographs to Mr. Popovic of -- I believe some of these photographs were already tendered. We will be using Sanction, although we're handing out hard copies of the photographs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, if you take a look at your monitor, just for the record I'd like to read out the ERN number, 01087882, and ask if you recognise this house.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Again, we have the problem of not knowing when these photographs were taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, these are, in part, pictures that were -- well, I shouldn't say in part. Actually, these are part of the photographs that were taken, as we discussed I think it was last week, in 1994 as part of a wider project, and we will have the photographers come in to testify about the date and the time and the exact exercise of taking the photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I suppose the best thing to do, because it's certainly much clearer, is that if you give the witness the photo itself rather than he follows on Sanction.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could take a look at ERN 01087882, I'll ask you if you recognise this photograph, this house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And look also at the state in which this house is, because at the end I'm also going to ask you some questions on how they ended up like this, whether you know when they ended up like this. Whose house is this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Golub Grujic's house. This is a man who worked as a merchant for a long time. This photograph was taken long after Christmas, because the new house had not yet been roofed over. The old house -- the new house did not have a roof at all, his house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And next, 884, 7884?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Savo Savljevic's house. This is between Kravica and Krajici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next, 7885.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Mika Grujic's house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next, 7886.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Stanoje Grujic's house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And where was this house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This house is, when you leave Bratunac, on the right-hand side, between Krajici and Kravica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next, 7887.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This house belonged to an elderly couple who had no children, Jovo and Zivana Miladzenovic [phoen].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next, 7888.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This house belongs to Rajko Milicevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When did you first see it in that condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 17th of March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next, 7890.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This house belongs to a man from Buljim who didn't reside in Kravica. He had left Kravica a long time ago, maybe 10 years before or so. I don't know his first and last name, but I know where the house is. It's plum in the center of Kravica, just next to the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next, 7892.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the center of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Next.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may just correct, it's 891, that last photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The previous one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, I don't have 891. I have 890 and then 892.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Oh, I see. That's fine, Your Honour. You can continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that was -- 892 is the center of Kravica, no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Next, 895.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is also the center of Kravica, a huge supermarket in Kravica, and to the left of the supermarket you can see Jevko Nikolic's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can just have a moment. I think the witness is looking at Sanction and then photographs are being handed to him, and I think there's a bit of confusion. So if we could just go back two photographs before and establish where he's looking -- I think it's best that the witness use the photographs at this point. I think Sanction is probably confusing things a bit. If the usher could give the witness 891.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is no 891, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: 892, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What's that? What's that showing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It used to be a shop first; next there was the post office, the local authority office, a health centre, then the Elektrodistribucija Company office. And then if you could show the center. So I've listed all these things - the shop, the post office, the local office, the health centre - and then there's another shot showing the cultural ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So when you saw this photo before, I heard you say this is the center in Kravica. Is it the center in Kravica? 892 I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we call this the center of Kravica, because this is where the post office was, the health centre, the shop, the grocery, and the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. 7895, those two buildings.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This house belongs to Zoran Ilic, and then here you can see a house belonging to the Popovic brothers, Cvijetin and Milos. They are my grandfather's relatives. And over here you can see Ceto Vasic's house that I spoke about a while ago. Djordjo ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I notice that one of these houses has a damaged roof; the other one doesn't have a roof at all, or at least not one that we can see. The one with the damaged roof, who did it belong to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Milos Popovic and Cvijetin Popovic, my grandfather's closest relatives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And to the left of it there is that white house with the chimney --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the chimney, that's Zoran Ilic's and Desimir Ilic's house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next, 896, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This house belongs to Rade Perisic and his brother Vidosav Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. 897.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This large house belongs to a man who used to work in Austria. Mile -- I can't remember his last name. Mile Milanovic, I believe. He and his three sons had been working in Austria for a long time. And then there was a man named Milanovic who was killed and then they had other relatives who moved to Kravica. Radomir Milanovic's family. This is my own meadow or field that you can see, with the corn stalks and the tall grass. That's my field. I have 10 acres all in all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have an idea at all -- I notice that on this photo there seems to be some reconstruction work going on. Would you have an idea at all as to which period this reconstruction work was being carried out? Which year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The reconstruction work was done in 1994, 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And if you look at the corn --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. Some of the houses further down, I helped people out to put up their roofs. The main thing was for the roofs to be constructed so no rain or snow got into the house. None of us were really handymen over there, we were all farmers. There must be more photographs. But people tried to roof their houses over, to build roofs, in 1994, whoever had slabs or tiles to use. This man who had worked in Austria, he paid people who were building the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I also noticed the corn plants, and you referred to them. What time of the year would you say this photo was taken? When would you expect the corn plants to be of that height in that part of the world?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is in July, because the corn had already been worked on. July or August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Next, 898.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the Kravica OKA. It was a shed where livestock was kept, cows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. 899.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is also part of the same building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I notice that on the -- in the background, on the left-hand side, there is another building. What was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is the same building, and there's another one right behind, next to the creek where the sheds were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So next is 7901. Whose house is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a house belonging to the church, where the church was in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which church? Orthodox church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The church, the Orthodox church, our church, the village church, and the house, the church house where the priest --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you ever see it in that condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. It's still like this. It hasn't been mended.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When did you see it in that condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first time I saw it like this, it might have been about the 18th or the 20th of March, when I went to the graveyard where my grandmother is buried and all of my family. My apologies. And then once we reached the graveyard, we passed by the church. The church had not been set fire to, but everything was torn down, and there was graffiti all over the walls. And then we reached the graveyard, and two or three graves had been dug up. The bodies had been taken out and placed beside the coffin, next to the grave. Then the -- the images on the gravestones had been smashed. My grandmother's image, it was pierced by bullets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's not relevant to this case. 904.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This house, it belongs to Cvijetin Dido from Bacici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There are three houses there. Let's start with the one on the left with a roof and no -- what seems to be no doors either.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This one belongs to Zoran Stevanovic, and right behind there's a creek. And then across the creek you see Zoran Stevanovic's house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the one in the middle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Cvijetin Dido's house. He's from the Bacici dam. And this other house belongs to his sons-in-law who live in Belgrade or in Novi Sad. It's a cottage that they use once every two or three months.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This house belongs to Bozo Milosevic. It's an old house, and a new house next to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. 908.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This one belongs to an elderly couple who had three children. They all worked in Germany. They also had another house in Zvornik, but they didn't stay in Kravica very often. Only when there was a holiday or some sort of a celebration, they'd come over with their kids for a barbecue, but they hardly ever came there. The man's name was Slavko and the wife's name was -- I can't remember her name, because they didn't reside in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you ever see this house in the condition that's shown on the picture, on the photo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's still like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When did you first see it like this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They died and the kids --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When did you first see it in that condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first time, when we came back to Kravica, so that is the 17th, 18th, and 19th of March, and onwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. 909.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This one belongs to Jefto Grujicic. It burned down to the ground. All you can see is the roof tiles. And the next one belongs to Ivo Popovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. 910. 910.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This house belongs to Pero Lasic. He owned three houses. You can see them all right here, the new one, the old one, and another one right here, some sort of a shed. Pero Lasic. It's the house next to mine; the distance is less than 30 metres, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the school building, the old school. This is the school building. The teachers lived here. This is the courtyard. That's what I told you about a while ago, where my father was captured. You can see the excavator, and you can see the corner of the school building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And the building on the right without the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the school building where the teachers who worked in the school lived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just wanted to make sure. I thought so. 914.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the gym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move to 918.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is my house. This is my old house. The bakery was here. This is my new house. What little roof is there, that's what I did, and my family now stays there. This is where the bakery used to be, and my old house ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why is he looking at 914 if I said 918?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so I can explain to you what has happened here with some of the photographs. Previously photographs were tendered through another witness, and so what we have done is not provided additional copies of those photographs, so the witness is now looking at photographs, I believe, that were not previously --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's cut it short. Show him 914, please. Usher, is that what he has in front of him? Yes. Could you tell us, whose house is that, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is my house, the old house where the bakery used to be, and this is the new house next to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. 918.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a house in a street that we called Devocukanja [phoen]. This is all from the village of Stuljici. The people who came over and bought up land here, their brothers and closest relatives. There are nine houses in a row here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. 920.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Neno Bozic's house. He's an old merchant who worked for a long time as a merchant. He now lives in Sabac. He bought a house there. Here I paid for the handyman to do some repairs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. 921.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Djordjo Milosevic's house, and the next one is Pavo Nikolic's house, and the other one is Golub Kojic's house. He is now in Germany.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's start with the left and go to the right. The one on the left, next to the electricity pole, whose house was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Golub Kojic's house. He lives in Germany with his family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the next one in the middle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Djordjo Milosevic's house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the one to the right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pavle Jankovic's house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next, 922, please. Whose house is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This roofless house belongs to Milo Milic. This other one belongs to Zdravko Milanovic, and the next house belongs to his brother, Jovan Milanovic. And the one you can see right here belongs to a close relative of his, Vitomir Milanovic, who was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt. Just before we complete - and I know we're running short on time - there are two additional photos that the witness did not have a chance to identify and they were previously tendered to the Court, so if I could just give the usher these two photographs for him to identify. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Put them on the ELMO, please, so that we know what we're talking about. Do you have the exhibit number, Ms. Richardson, of this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: It's actually on the ELMO. It's P400, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: P400, you are being told.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, do you recognise that house or those buildings over there? Whose house was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, that was Pero Nikolic's house, right across the road from my old house where the bakery was. There were two shops here from the '60s, two big shops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the center of Kravica that I talked about; the community centre, the post office, the local office, the shop, the health centre, then the electrical supply ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. For the record, the witness is being shown the photo with the ERN ending in 7891. Do you know the exhibit number of this document, Ms. Richardson?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it is P400. P400, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: P400, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have two very short questions. You've seen a lot of houses, a lot of photos depicting a lot of houses. When you returned to Kravica after the attack, did you see all these houses on that occasion or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did, all of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And were they all in the condition in which they appear on this photo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Even worse. There are houses here that have been roofed over, so this is not a picture taken between the 17th and 20th of March, when we arrived in our village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was there any of these houses, on the 17th or 20th of March, which were not damaged at all, or which were much less damaged than what appears on these photos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We found the houses in a state worse than the state in the photographs, because some houses have been roofed over since then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Ms. Richardson, please, the witness is yours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, with respect to compensation, did you receive, or anyone else that you know of in the village of Kravica receive any compensation from the Bosnian Muslim army for damage?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I have to restate my objection to that question. There's no such thing as the Bosnian Muslim army, and we'll never hear of it anywhere or see a document mentioning the Bosnian Muslim army. If the Prosecution wants to deny that there was a Republic of Bosnia --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think I have to sustain the objection. Could you rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And by the way, these photos are being given which number, Mr. Registrar? P458?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be P459.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 459. This set of photos is P459.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution simply needs to ask, Have you received any compensation. They don't need to add any tag.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that it's the Prosecution's contention that the damage from the attack was caused by Bosnian Muslim forces, and I can simply ask if he was compensated by any Muslim forces of any kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just ask him whether he has been compensated, and if he has been, he will need to tell us who compensated him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: We can take that route, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever compensated for the loss to your home, Mr. Popovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Either the loss of your home or any damage sustained on the occasion of the attack.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have received nothing. My house and the four outbuildings, my barn with three cows and two calves, about 20 pigs, 15 sheep, a small tractor with various equipment for mowing, plowing, and so on, the things in my house, everything that a household needs, we had. I never received anything. After '94/'95 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That will be enough. So you haven't even receive anything from Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't understand anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I will repeat my question. So basically what you're telling us is that you didn't even receive anything from Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I never received any kind of compensation from anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. Please may I? I haven't finished. An organisation turned up, they were Hungarians, and they were helping about the houses in Kravica. And I received a little bit of building material. It was some gravel which was cheap in our parts. And I received that from a foreign country, from Hungarians who were there helping people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Ms. Richardson, any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I am proceeding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did there come a time that you saw the village of Kravica after the attack on television or on video?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Somebody brought a videotape to our village, and this was taken by the Muslims. The tape showed Naser Oric with a horse in front of the community centre. He was riding a horse, and there were soldiers around him. And then they showed in Srebrenica how they were engaging in sports --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, stop, stop. Do you have this tape?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am leading into a photograph that is, I think, very similar to what is being described.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But a tape is a tape and a photo is a photo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: We are looking into getting this video, Your Honour, which is why I'm also leading this evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Excuse me, until the Prosecution obtains the video, they should surely stick to the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But at least they can give us a description of this video. Let him give us a description of this video so that when we get it, if we get it, we'll be able to mix and match.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: That was my intent, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. You saw this video yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw it myself, in my house. My mother wept. Somebody brought this to the village. It went from house to house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you keep a copy of it, or did you make a copy of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't. I didn't think I'd ever need it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you know of anyone who can provide us with a copy of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really can't make any promises now. It was a long time ago. When people were returning to Kravica, we watched this. So I can't promise you anything for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, you mentioned that Naser Oric was on a horse. How do you know that was Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you know how? I knew Naser a little bit before the war, when he would come to Kravica with his Renault to see Paco Vlasic, who was a car mechanic. And when he talked to him, this car mechanic afterwards would say, That's Naser who used to work in Belgrade in the SUP, and now he's been transferred to Srebrenica. We had no idea. This was before the war, a short time before the war. He would come to Kravica with his Renault.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: -- I'd like to hand up this photograph, copies of the photograph that will be shown to the witness. For the record, it's ERN 03592926, and I'd ask that a number be assigned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the source of this document, Ms. Richardson?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document was provided to the Office of the Prosecution, by the RS Banja Luka to one of our investigators. We also received it from the Bureau of Cooperation, the RS Bureau of Cooperation as well. And this was provided to our investigators. So there are two sources. And I would like to add an additional source, which is the fact that this photograph is in the public domain, and that it was also retrieved, the same photograph, from an Internet source, an encyclopedia Internet source, and I can have copies of that source handed out to the Court as well as the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, your question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Popovic, have a look at this photograph. And we are also showing the photograph on Sanction. And we will just ask you if you recognise where this photograph -- if you've seen this photograph before.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see -- in front of the community centre in Kravica, this videotape I talked about, where these people are, that's where that video was taken from, in the middle of the asphalt. You could see Naser on a horse, and the soldiers all around him, just like you see here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see no horse there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can, Sanction, we will sort of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: -- get a closer shot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, I see a horse.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And we can put the photograph back to the original size for the moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise anyone in the picture? Let's have it blown up again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I wonder if Sanction can also make the horse white.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is an inappropriate comment from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you recognise anyone in the photograph, Mr. Popovic?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The picture on the videotape was just like this one. Naser was on a horse, only it was taken by a video camera from where they are, and he was on the asphalt. And as I just explained, above the asphalt there's a house. This man lives in Serbia. I don't remember him ever actually living in that house. So there's an asphalt surface there, and then there's a hill, and then there's the house on that hill. And it was taken from in front of the community centre, here where we see them now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, look at the faces in the photograph, and could you tell us if you recognise anyone in that photo.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recognise anyone. This picture is blurred. You can't see very well. But I do know that on the videotape, I saw this very clearly, as if it was live. But here, I can't recognise anyone here because it is blurred. But it was just like this, with Naser on a horse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just a moment. I want to make sure what he was looking at. Were you looking at the photo on the piece of paper or on the monitor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the video cassette in my house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That wasn't the question. Conclude on this, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the photograph on the ELMO and tell me if you can identify anyone in the photograph. Don't look at the screen in front of you, on the ELMO. The hard copy. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here I recognise Naser on the horse, because that's how I saw it on the videotape. On the videotape, you could see it much more clearly, you could see it very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, looking at this photograph, is this the person that you recognise from previously visiting Kravica? The person on the horse.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this man here, he has a beard. But when he used to come to Kravica, he didn't have a beard. Also, this picture is not very clear, so I cannot see the picture very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't look like this with a beard when he visited Kravica with his Renault.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just have the Court's indulgence for one moment. If we could go back at that Sanction and again just go to the person on the horse, see if we can enlarge it and if that assists the witness any further. If it doesn't, fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, please look at the video -- the screen and tell us if this will assist you any further in recognising the person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The more you zoom, the more blurred it becomes.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. This person on the horse is Naser Oric, and you can see the same on the video cassette, except there he's on the asphalt, not here in the center of Kravica. But on the video cassette, you can see him five metres away from this spot, just like this, sitting on a horse. And it was shot with a video cassette from the position where these soldiers are now, and in the background you can see the hill and the house on the top of the hill and the asphalt area that I just described.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. This will be Prosecution Exhibit 460.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell from the photograph - thank you, Your Honour - what time of year this photograph was taken? Can you tell the weather conditions, if there's snow on the ground or not?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in those days when Kravica was taken. On the 7th of January, there was a lot of snow, and you can see snow here. So it was from the 7th of January onwards. There was a lot of snow then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I have no further questions with respect to the photograph, and I thank the usher --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it you have no further questions about anything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have two questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's conclude, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: -- and I'll conclude.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, are you a member of the SDS? And can you tell us if you are active in the SDS?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not a member of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the only other question --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Were you a member of the SDS in 1991 and 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: You're welcome, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Madam Vidovic, let's start, and then we'll see where we get.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will start with a set of questions. Cross-examined by Ms. Vidovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Popovic. Please, after I finish my question, make a brief pause because time is needed for the interpreters so that everybody can hear us. Did you understand what I said?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, do you have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it Cojka?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cojo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your nickname is Cojo.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Mr. Popovic, are you aware that on Tuesday, Mr. Ratko Nikolic said to the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, we don't do it this way. You don't tell him what another witness said.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But now you have said it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you give to any witness any documents pertaining to the Naser Oric case?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You mean that I showed this to someone?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I mean did you at any time give any documents connected with the Naser Oric case to any of the witnesses appearing before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never showed them any documents. I only asked Ratko -- when we met, he was passing through Kravica on a horse with a forwarding agent, and so he stopped and we had a chat, and I said, Ratko, when were you taken prisoner in Kravica. And he said on the 12th, on the 12th, at home. And then I said, No, Ratko, you weren't captured on the 12th, it was on the 9th. After that I never saw Ratko or talked to him again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Let's clear this up. Did you ever -- did you ever give Ratko any documents, or did you ever show him any documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, never, never. I never showed him anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Neither did you give him any documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Go on -- go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, do you know Ratko Nikolic well?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he a person who can be trusted, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Objection --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Objection -- don't answer it. Objection sustained.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please, when answering my question just a minute ago in connection with this gentleman, when I asked you about your conversation, you said, He told me he had been arrested on the 12th and I told him on the 9th. Why were you suggesting anything at all to Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because Ratko can't be trusted about dates. I don't know personally when he was arrested. I don't know. I didn't give him any documents. We met only about three times after.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But why did you say that you can't trust Ratko just now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He did not say that you can't trust Ratko; he said that you can't trust Ratko with dates.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I hope that "dates" means day, month, and year, and not other dates.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you suggest anything to Ratko?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what did I tell Ratko? I didn't say anything, I didn't give Ratko any documents. What did I give him?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you suggest anything to Ratko about his arrest?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean I shouldn't have talked to Ratko at all?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please. Yes, it was all right for you to talk to him, but why did you suggest to him anything about facts in connection with the Naser Oric case, having to do with his arrest, the arrest of Mr. Nikolic, that is?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you suggest to him that it was the 9th and not the 12th?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What did I ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you just said that you suggested to him that he had not been arrested on the 12th but rather on the 9th. Why did you suggest this to him? Is there any reason why you mentioned that this was the 9th?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was talking in Kravica that he had been arrested on the 17th of January, the 9th, the 12th. He was lost as far as dates was concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how did you know when he was arrested?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea when he was arrested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present at his arrest?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why, then, did you suggest to Nikolic that he had been arrested on another day and not the day when he said he had been arrested? Isn't it correct, in fact, that you are trying to interfere in the process of international justice, that you are trying to influence others?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why would I influence other people? Why would I do that? How could I influence them?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's correct that you didn't give him those documents, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't give any document to Ratko Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it would not be true to say that you gave him documents.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't give Ratko any kind of document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I'll move on now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know if I should move on to my next set of questions, because I'm very short of time, or -- I feel this is a very important issue. I don't know whether the Chamber wishes to put questions about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: About what he's just stated?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We're happy with what he said. This is an adversarial system. We'll have a break of 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this would be a convenient time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And then we'll restart in 25 minutes, and then you choose when you prefer to stop, Ms. Vidovic, and we will obviously continue tomorrow because this is an important witness, all right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's proceed, please, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, did I understand you correctly when you said you were not a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The truth of the matter is, you were a member of the SDS from the 26th of August, 1990, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's not correct, is it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please have the usher's assistance now. I would like to place the following document on the ELMO: It's a Bratunac military post document, dated the 6th of April, 1995. This is a certificate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, if you could please have a look. This document is a certificate of the Bratunac military post, certifying as follows: "Nikola Popovic has been in our unit from 18 April 1992 until 23 September 1992 and from 25 May 1993 until the present day and onwards." This certificate is issued at the personal request to regulate accommodation issues. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to that I would like to ask you a question: Is it true that you were mobilised on the 18th of April, 1992, and that you remained with the army of Republika Srpska until the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which date did you refer to, the 18th?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you look at the document, please. Is it true that on the 18th of April, 1992, you were mobilised?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't be sure. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Eser, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I just have a question for clarification. You asked the witness whether he was a member of the SDS, and he gave an answer no, and then you continued by presenting this document. Now, is this document related to the question with regard to the membership in the SDS, or is there a different issue?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, after that I said "very well, thank you." I'm not sure if it's been interpreted or not. And then I moved on to a different topic and asked this question about his being mobilised. Maybe you did not receive this particular bit of interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something in connection with the SDS after you've given me this?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is not in relation to the SDS. I asked you a different question. We'll go back to the SDS in a while. Can you please just answer my questions. We will come back to the SDS. I asked you about the certificate, about you being mobilised, and I asked you when exactly. You say you didn't remember; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was in the army, I don't know. It was in April or May 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough. Thank you. That is a satisfactory answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to verify this, Your Honour. Has this document already been assigned a number as a Defence exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. I don't think so. I've never seen it before. We had similar ones, but not this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Therefore, I move that this document be assigned a number as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document is being tendered, received, and marked as Defence Exhibit D122? 122.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A while ago you mentioned the bakery. When asked by the Prosecutor on Tuesday, you said, "I worked as a baker. When the war began, the bakery was built of wood and it catered to the entire village. We baked bread there, and all the locals came to the bakery for their bread. It catered for the entire village of Kravica." Mr. Nikolic, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this a civilian bakery?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a village bakery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough. Thank you. In your testimony, you referred to a person named Andrija Jerkovic. Where is this person from?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jerkovici. Jerkovici, which belongs to the Bacici. Brana Bacici. But the hamlet is called Jerkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's part of Brana Bacici?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that in your area, around Kravica, tensions began to rise when Andrija Jerkovic was wounded in May 1992, and around mid-May Stojan Popovic was killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In answer to a question by the Honourable Judge today in relation to Glogova - that's page 24 of the LiveNote, line 1 - your answer was as follows: "I know that before the war Glogova was a Muslim village, but it was cleansed at the beginning of the war." Can you please explain to the Chamber what this means,"cleansed"? What exactly happened there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what happened there. Glogova was not part of Kravica. It's closer to Bratunac. I know nothing about that, about what happened at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did say today, didn't you, that Glogova was cleansed. What exactly did you mean by that expression, "cleansed"?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That there were no Muslims. That it was cleansed, so that the Muslims had left Glogova. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When someone leaves, is "cleansing" the proper expression to use for these cases?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure exactly how it should be used. I'm not ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you say that Glogova was cleansed, then?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe the witness has already answered the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, he hasn't. By no means, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By no means.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, Witness, can you tell us, how far is Glogova from Kravica?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Kravica?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About eight kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the distance between Brana Bacici and Kravica?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About seven or eight kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know exactly, don't you, what happened to Andrija Jerkovic. Does it not seem logical that you should know what happened in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's because Andrija Jerkovic was wounded in the area of Kravica. It's a hamlet which is part of Kravica, and Glogova isn't. Glogova belonged to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me what the distance is between Hranca and Kravica?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which Hranca? There is Gornja Hranca and Donja Hranca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ten kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's in your neighbourhood, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean by "neighbourhood"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The area in which you live.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you by any chance hear that in Hranca, Glogova, Suha, Borkovac, Voljevica, Magasici, Mihajlovici, hundreds if not actually thousands of Muslims were killed at the time, at the same time that this person named Jerkovic was wounded?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never heard such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Never, and that's your testimony.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never heard any such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now if I can have the usher's assistance, please, I would like to place on the ELMO Defence Exhibit D7 -- oh, yes, D7, it's already there. This is a document that I've already elucidated on. It's an extract from the financial records. This is a list of staff members and logistics for the Kravica Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at this document, Witness. Your name, if indeed it is your name, is under number 17. It says "Nikola Popovic," doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that your name?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, you were a member of the logistics unit of the Kravica staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was a logistics person. Here you can see my name and this friend of mine who worked with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us exactly what you did between the 18th of April, 1992 and January 1993? What was your job with the staff?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked as a baker.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the staff?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, baker. A baker, a Kravica local baker.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if that was a civilian bakery, as you explained a while ago, what would be the connection between that and the staff?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the bakery catered for the entire village, bread for the entire village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough. Thank you. Can you please look at the document. If you could turn to the next page, it reads "Donji Bacici." Can you just go through the document briefly. You see here it reads "Artillery," and then there's a list of military conscripts for the village of Mandici on the next page. If you could just have a look briefly, first of all. The document has several pages, then Brezanci, Dolovi, then you have Siljkovici, Marici, Ceta Kravica, the Jezero position, Ocenovici, Banici, Popovici, Brana, and then you have a list of military conscripts for the village of Opravdici, Jezestica 2, Jezestica 1, the village of Magasici, Kajici. Yesterday you marked a map during your testimony. If you could have a look, please. I'm only talking about the place names here, indicated here.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You made markings on a map here yesterday.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it not true that you marked exactly the villages that I have referred to now? Aren't these all Serb villages?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I hate to interrupt, but just for the record, it wasn't yesterday but Monday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honour. My apologies. Tuesday, as a matter of fact. Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, I'm not confused just because you're looking at me. Can you please answer the following question: Is it not true that these villages had their own military units? If you could look at this list in relation to Donji Bacici, for example, or Siljkovici, for that matter, if you could have a look. Can you find Siljkovici on the list, please.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why don't you refer him straight to the page, Madam Vidovic, instead of --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will give the reference. If you could look at page 0132-0329, the block letters.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could draw your attention to Siljkovici specifically. Because you mentioned Siljkovici today, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but can I just read the names out, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead, please. I can read them out to you out aloud for the benefit of the transcript: Peric Radoljub, Krsmanovic Dusan -- and you try to follow -- Stevanovic Milan, Savljevic Brano, Radovic Milovan, Perisic Obren, Djokic Stanoje --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think you are expecting too much. Please slow down. How far did you get?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Obren Perisic, Stanoje Djokic, Gojko Grujic, Stanko Grujic, Ratko Peric, and especially I'd like to draw your attention to the names of the Radovic family, who you spoke about today.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Radovic family, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The persons that you referred to, Radovic Sveto, Radovic Bozo, Radovic Novak, Radovic Zeljko?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Vaskrsija Radovic?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vaskrsija, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Radovic Radojko?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Radovic Radojko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Radovic Slobodan? Radovic Milorad?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, it is the list I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... continue like this I'm going to stop the sitting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Am I allowed to say something in relation to this list?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you just pause for a minute and I'll ask you a question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You will answer questions. You will not make statements. And Madam Vidovic, please, again for the third, fourth time, please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We haven't even -- it was going too fast even for me to follow. She didn't mention all the names, she mentioned some of them. And you had arrived at putting the question. You said that the persons you referred to, Radovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Radovic Milovan, Radovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And then it's --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the Radovic family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please, are these the persons that you referred to today in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it not true that these persons were soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were persons from Kravica who defended their village when it was attacked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these people who were members of the Siljkovici military unit?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Siljkovici military unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they were defending their village, that's who these people were.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I may be allowed to finish answering.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
