utterances.text: Can you please just answer my questions.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, half of these people did not take part in the war, the people that I know of, those people had left. This is a list of people from Siljkovici, but not people who were actually in positions in Siljkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I asked you something in relation to specific members of the Radovic family which you referred to today, and your answer was what it was. Now can you please tell me, which of these people left?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are people who left, there are people who were aged over 60. I'll tell you now which specific people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please now, may I, for the last time, appeal to you not to cross over while one is still talking; and secondly, to allow for a good pause, a reasonable pause between question and answer. If you do not do this, I'm going to stop the sitting. Judge Eser would like to put a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Just for reason of clarification, because I'm not sure whether the translation is -- all of it is consistent. So if you speak of -- if you've got military units, is it meant in terms of the army; and if so, what army? Is it meant in terms of Territorial Defence? Or is it meant in terms of village guard? What means "military unit"?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I asked the witness a question, was this a military unit, was it a village guard, and he's the one who should answer my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a village guard, people who defended their village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you call it a village guard? Was it a village guard of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who it belonged to. I know that it was a village guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but a Serb village guard, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Serb, what else? Those people were Serbs, not Muslims. They all have Serb first and last names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. A while ago --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, you yourself are not allowing a pause.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honour, but I always have very little time left for my cross-examination; therefore, I'm trying to squeeze as many questions as possible into the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I haven't said anything about your cross-examination time. I haven't said anything. You will finish your cross-examination when you finish. But at 7.00 in the evening, I have an absolute duty to protect the staff here who has been behind windows and small cubicles interpreting and translating. It's not an easy life at all for them. It's not for us, but for us it's even worse.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can I re-ask this question, please: In answer to the questions by the OTP today, the persons you referred to as being members of the village guard or village defence, you spoke of them as soldiers, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said was that it was a village guard and a defence line. Therefore, you couldn't have a woman going there, for example. It could only have been a man, a soldier, defending the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough. I'll ask you a different question now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: A very small matter, Your Honour, but I've noticed that "dobro" gets translated as "fair enough," and it's simply that "fair enough" implies that we've accepted that as a fair answer. "Dobro" in this context, it would be better as "okay" or something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's how I know it. Okay, point taken, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's correct, is it not, Witness, that the hamlets belonging to Kravica that you marked on the map yesterday, that from the very beginning of the war, these hamlets had their own village guards, as you called them, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village guards were in the center of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These villages, did they have village guards too? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about those villages. I know about Kravica and the center of Kravica, what was there. I don't know about Buljim. That's 15 or 10 kilometres from Kravica. I have no idea whether they had a village guard too. I know about Kravica, where the post office used to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you remember that you gave a statement to the OTP in July 2004; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke then about between 250 and 300 fighters, as you referred to them, who were in Kravica, which, as you then said, included the quartermasters' staff. That means between 250 and 300 fighters were in Kravica itself, weren't they? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not in Kravica itself, the villages, because up until the beginning of the war, Christmas 1993, many people had been killed and many people had left and many people had been wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, but you just said a moment ago that you had no idea what happened in those villages, how many soldiers they had.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know when a man from Bacici was killed. I hear that these people were killed or wounded or that they left. How on earth should I know whether they had a village guard or not in their own village?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, my question to you is: When you said that Kravica had between 250 and 300 fighters, what exactly did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Able-bodied men, at Christmas, to defend the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you referred to Kravica itself and not to the surrounding hamlets, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The surrounding hamlets included between 250 -- and the men who were on the line when Kravica came under attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm still not asking any questions about the attack on Kravica, I'm simply asking about the situation before the attack. To the best of your knowledge, how many members of the village guards were there in the surrounding villages?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Kravica?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kravica, 40 people who defended the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you say that there were between 250 and 300 in your statement in July?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my estimate. I know how many villages there were, and at that time Kravica came under attack, I thought that was a fair figure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to now take you back to this document, if you could please look at page 0132-0326. Again, it says "Donji Bacici," and then it reads "Artillery." Do you agree, sir, that artillery personnel are people who operate artillery weapons?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea who they are. I've never been in the army. I have no idea what that means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at the list. Do you recognise any of these names? Do you know any of these persons?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Donji Bacici?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Slow down, Witness, please.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Donji Bacici?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you please look at this column under the heading "Artillery Men," if you could please look at the names, or "Gunners," as the document says. Do you know any of these persons?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know these people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where these persons were deployed between May 1992 and the 7th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where they were deployed, but they were all in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, all these people are locals from Kravica, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Witness. Thank you. Witness, are you aware of the fact that Siljkovici had artillery?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had an artillery piece; I don't know whether it was a mortar or something else. But yes, they did have a mortar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you do know what artillery is, don't you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I heard about it. I heard about a mortar. I never saw it, nor did I ever handle one. But I heard that there was a mortar at Siljkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecutor, on Tuesday, asked you whether the defence lines in Kravica were held only by men from Kravica, that is, local people.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you confirmed this.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your testimony, then, that there were no volunteers from Serbia there and no people from various other units in various places?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that. Soldiers did come to assist us from Bratunac. When there was a large-scale attack, they would stay a day or two until things quietened down, and then they would go back to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Only from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know about those from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that there were many volunteers from Serbia who had come from Stara Pazova, for example, at the beginning of the war?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know these people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to ask the usher to put on the ELMO document 02 -- to hand to the witness document 0207-5896. This is an excerpt from a document of the Bratunac military post, which begins with 0207-5870 to 0207-5956. At present what is relevant for us is only the present document. I just wanted to state what its origin was, which is why I read the first and last ERN numbers of the entire document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would like to ask the usher to put for a moment on the ELMO the Prosecutor's map, P455.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wait, wait, wait, we are not receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please take another look at this map which you indicated things on yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember, witness, that you yesterday you marked for the Prosecutor on the map you have before you the village of Sandici.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show it to Their Honours once again.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]. Here it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village of Sandici is a Muslim village, is it not?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that it was very close to this line that you drew yesterday --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- as the line of defence of your village?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at this document now, please.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please bear with me a little. I only wish to obtain answers to questions I need to ask. I need to get your answers to these questions. Please look at these names. You have 17 names here. The names are followed by the year of birth and the address. This document is entitled "List of Persons Killed in Sandici." When you look at the dates of death, would you agree that the first 13 were killed in Sandici on the 24th of May, 1992? 1992, I do apologise, the 29th of May, 1992. I may have misspoken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, and it's not the first 13, but the first 11, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first 11 were killed on the 29th of May, 1992. Witness, now please take a look at these villages and tell Their Honours --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I say something about these men?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Please answer my questions. If the Trial Chamber later permits you to say something else, then you may later on. Please, under number 6, Dragica Mastikosa from Novi Sad, killed on the 29th of May, 1992, in Sandici; Vesna Krdzalic, on the 29th of May, 1992, in Sandici. Novi Sad is a town in Serbia, is it not?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mile Vorkapic from Tenje; Jovanovic Zarko from Medulin; Grahovac Aleksandar from Borovo Masilje [phoen]; Muljadin Doljanovic [phoen] from Beli Manastir. Is it not correct, Witness, that these are towns in the Serbian Krajina, towns outside of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were these people doing in Sandici at your defence line on the 29th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you know what happened on the 26th, when the villages were taken? This was the return of the village. Your Honour, may I answer this question. First I arrived here to testify about my father and my grandfather --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but you answer the questions that are put to you, Mr. Popovic. What do you want to tell us about -- he is not receiving interpretation, he's saying. Can you receive interpretation now? Can you receive interpretation now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, now I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. What did you want to tell the Trial Chamber about these persons on this list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to say that on the 26th of May, the villages of Mratinci, Dornji and Gornji, and Dolovi, and Buljim, Jerkovici, were burned down, and then three days later we wanted to recapture these villages. And these people were killed in Sandici; that's what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic, I suggest you close on this, because you've got five minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll put this to you. Vesna Krdzalic and Vesna Mastikosa are women?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they fought there, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly not in Kravica. They were never in Kravica. I don't know where they came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever heard that these women were very prominent in the ethnic cleansing of Glogova?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear about that. I didn't go to Glogova or to Bratunac. I spent the entire time in Kravica. I don't know what happened in those places.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to conclude for today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This document will be marked Defence Exhibit D123. So we stand adjourned until tomorrow morning at -- yes, Ms. Richardson, what's the problem?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: No problem, Your Honour. We do have some information to disclose to the Defence, and perhaps it would be best if the witness were not present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can disclose it when we finish. We don't even need to be present ourselves, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: No, you do not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So, Witness, you will be escorted and returned to your hotel. I'm sure that within an hour tomorrow, we will be finished. Have a pleasant evening. We stand adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9.00. If I am not feeling well tomorrow, I will ask Judge Brydensholt and Judge Eser to conduct the sitting, the two of them, in my absence, in terms of Rule 15(A). But I'll try to recover as much as I can by tomorrow morning so that I can be present, but I don't promise anything, because I'm feeling much worse than I was this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 10th day of December, 2004, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.58 p.m.,
